author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

  as a follow-up request.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader sees every specialty with the veterinarians holding it
summary: A read-only specialty directory page lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it, all on one page. Reachable at its own address only.
acceptance_criteria: The page is served at the address /specialties.html.
Given the specialties the clinic knows, when the page is opened, then every one of them is listed by its stored name.
Given a specialty one or more veterinarians hold, when the page is opened, then each holder is shown by first name then last name, for example "Helen Leary".
Given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when the page is opened, then it is listed as held by none.
Given a veterinarian holding no specialty, when the page is opened, then that veterinarian is not shown anywhere on it.
Given every specialty the clinic knows, when the page is opened, then all of them are shown together, with no paging control.
Given a clinic that knows no specialty, when the page is opened, then it renders empty rather than failing.
Specialties are listed in a stable order, and so are the veterinarians under each.
Wording the page introduces is present in every language the clinic supports and is not fixed to one language (REQ-LANG-002).
No other page links to the new page, and no navigation entry is added for it.
non_goals: Creating, changing, or removing veterinarians or specialties from the page (NG-2 unchanged)
A navigation entry for the page, or a link to it from any other page
Paging, filtering, or searching within the page
Listing veterinarians who hold no specialty
notes: Boundary check: no Non-Goals row changes, so no scope_overrides. NG-2 holds unchanged (read-only view). NG-9 (only owners are searchable) holds: the page lists, it does not search. REQ-SYS-001 holds: the new page carries the existing navigation like every page, but gains no entry of its own. Three questions stayed open under the owner's standing instruction and are recorded in the PRD Open Questions: a visible entry point (deferred to a possible follow-up request), the ordering rule (narrow reading: stable, not named), and two specialties stored under one name (narrow reading: one entry per stored specialty).

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice lands entirely inside the vet feature package and needs design ground the durable memory does not yet hold. Two properties of the current model force it: the Vet-to-Specialty association is mapped one way only, so no type answers 'who holds this specialty', and a specialty nobody holds is reachable from no veterinarian. The page therefore needs a second read source (a SpecialtyRepository over the existing specialties table) and an inversion step. That inversion is recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-17-specialty-directory-read-model.md and realized as a stateless domain service, adopted from the 'Available, not currently used' row of the pattern catalog in docs/architecture-principles.md. Placement, naming, rendering, and persistence all follow existing rules: feature-package organization (ADR 2026-07-31-feature-package-organization), server-side Thymeleaf with externalized text (ADR 2026-07-31-server-side-rendering-with-thymeleaf), and direct JPA mapping on the domain types (ADR 2026-07-31-relational-persistence-with-spring-data-jpa). No schema change on any of the three vendors: the specialties table and the vet_specialties join table already exist. Basis for the claims about existing symbols is a direct read of every file in src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/vet plus PetTypeRepository, CacheConfiguration, fragments/layout.html, and vets/vetList.html; the IDE oracle is not connected in this run, so this is the weaker grep-class basis.
integration_points: New GET route /specialties.html served from the vet package by SpecialtyController; the existing VetController is left untouched, so each controller adapts one HTTP surface.
SpecialtyRepository is a new Spring Data repository over the existing specialties table; no schema, seed-data, or entity-mapping change on H2, MySQL, or PostgreSQL.
The page reuses VetRepository.findAll(), which is @Cacheable("vets") and eager-fetches each vet's specialties; no second cache is introduced and CacheConfiguration is unchanged.
The template lives under templates/vets/ and renders through the shared fragments/layout.html layout fragment, like every other page.

The layout fragment's menu argument selects which navigation entry is highlighted. Pass a value matching no existing menu item so the page highlights nothing and layout.html gains no entry — the acceptance criterion forbidding a navigation entry is satisfied by not editing layout.html at all.

Message keys: prefer the existing keys that already fit (specialties, vets, none) over new wording. Any key the page does introduce must be added to messages.properties and to every translated bundle; I18nPropertiesSyncTest fails the build on a missing key and on literal text in a template (messages_en is exempt by fallback).

patterns.description: The lookup-repository shape to mirror: a declarative Spring Data interface returning every row of a lookup table in name order. SpecialtyRepository is the same shape for Specialty.

Reuse verbatim: first-name-then-last-name rendering (${vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName}) and the #{none} fallback for an empty specialty cell. The directory inverts the axes but needs no new rendering idiom.
Controller test shape: @WebMvcTest on the single controller, @MockitoBean for the repositories, MockMvc asserting status, model attribute, and view name.

Pattern catalog: Domain service is adopted from the 'Available, not currently used' list, which the brief allows without an ADR. Naming rule for that row is a verb or action name, stateless — hence GroupVeterinariansBySpecialty rather than a noun. SpecialtyHolders is a value object under the closed properties: immutable, equal by value, defensive copy of the holder list. The persistence-entity exception does not cover it, because the framework does not instantiate it.

risks.risk: Grouping logic drifting into SpecialtyController. The checklist in docs/architecture-principles.md states that a new rule added to a web controller is a fresh violation, not covered by the existing controller-logic deviation.
risks.mitigation: GroupVeterinariansBySpecialty owns the inversion. The controller calls the two repositories, delegates, puts the result in the model, and returns the view name — nothing else. Five of the six acceptance criteria are then unit-testable against real Vet and Specialty objects with no web or JPA context, which is where the bulk of the tests belong.

risks.risk: Unstable ordering. The requirement asks for a stable order for specialties and for the holders under each; two specialties may be stored under the same name, and two veterinarians may share a name.
risks.mitigation: Sort specialties by name with the stored identity as tiebreaker, and holders by last name then first name then identity. Every sort key is total, so the page is deterministic for any data set.

risks.risk: Two specialties stored under one name collapsing into one entry. The narrow reading recorded in the PRD is one entry per stored specialty.
risks.mitigation: Group by the specialty's stored identity, never by its name. Note that Specialty inherits equals/hashCode from the entity hierarchy — if grouping uses a Map keyed by Specialty, confirm the key semantics rather than assuming them, or key by identifier explicitly.

risks.risk: Unbounded read. The page has no paging by requirement and loads every specialty and every veterinarian on each request.
risks.mitigation: Accepted and recorded in the ADR's Consequences. The result set is bounded by the clinic's roster, and the veterinarian read goes through the existing cache. No mitigation is designed in; the risk is stated so a future data-volume change reopens it.

risks.risk: Stale data from the vet cache. VetRepository's reads are cached with no eviction configured (open question 5 in docs/system-design.md).
risks.mitigation: Inherited, not worsened: the directory reads the same cache the vet list already reads, and NG-2 keeps the page read-only with no write path to invalidate. Do not add a specialties cache — that would need a new cache declaration in CacheConfiguration and would widen the same open question.

risks.risk: Build failure from I18nPropertiesSyncTest on hard-coded page text or a key missing from one of the translated bundles.
risks.mitigation: Every visible string goes through #{...}. If a new key is needed, add it to messages.properties and to all nine translated bundles in the same change (messages_en is exempt by fallback).

risks.risk: Lazy-loading failure while rendering, since spring.jpa.open-in-view is disabled.
risks.mitigation: Vet.specialties is mapped FetchType.EAGER, so the graph the page needs is loaded inside the repository call. The read model is assembled before rendering, so the template touches no persistence proxy.

notes: Security: the slice introduces no new trust boundary. The route is a GET with no path variables, no query parameters, and no form binding, so there is no input to validate at the boundary. It discloses nothing new — veterinarian names and specialty names are both already public on /vets.html. Output escaping is Thymeleaf's default: use th:text throughout and never th:utext. The page is unauthenticated like every other route, which is the recorded posture of this demonstration application (docs/system-design.md § Security Context), not a new gap. Reliability: one request, two read-only repository calls, no blocking I/O beyond the datasource, nothing long-running to cancel; an empty specialties table renders an empty table rather than failing. Durable-memory writes this dispatch made: new ADR docs/adr/2026-08-17-specialty-directory-read-model.md and its index row; four Contracts rows in docs/system-design.md carrying REQ-SPECIALTYDIRECTORY-001; an Overview sentence naming the domain service as the one exception to the no-service-layer shape; a Contracts note that Specialty carries no back-reference; the first Implementation Order row; one banner sentence marking post-survey statements as designed state. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit found nothing to judge. Open question carried forward, not raised to the human under the standing instruction: the requirement's word 'holder' is not yet a term in docs/ubiquitous-language.md, which defines Specialty as 'held by' veterinarians. SpecialtyHolders and GroupVeterinariansBySpecialty use that wording. Whether 'holder' joins the canonical vocabulary is the product expert's call; the design does not depend on the answer, and no code name changes if it is added.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader sees every specialty with the veterinarians holding it
summary: A read-only specialty directory page lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it, all on one page. Reachable at its own address only.
acceptance_criteria: The page is served at the address /specialties.html.
Given the specialties the clinic knows, when the page is opened, then every one of them is listed by its stored name.
Given a specialty one or more veterinarians hold, when the page is opened, then each holder is shown by first name then last name, for example "Helen Leary".
Given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when the page is opened, then it is listed as held by none.
Given a veterinarian holding no specialty, when the page is opened, then that veterinarian is not shown anywhere on it.
Given every specialty the clinic knows, when the page is opened, then all of them are shown together, with no paging control.
Given a clinic that knows no specialty, when the page is opened, then it renders empty rather than failing.
Specialties are listed in a stable order, and so are the veterinarians under each.
Wording the page introduces is present in every language the clinic supports and is not fixed to one language (REQ-LANG-002).
No other page links to the new page, and no navigation entry is added for it.
non_goals: Creating, changing, or removing veterinarians or specialties from the page (NG-2 unchanged)
A navigation entry for the page, or a link to it from any other page
Paging, filtering, or searching within the page
Listing veterinarians who hold no specialty

risks.risk: Grouping logic drifting into SpecialtyController. The checklist in docs/architecture-principles.md states that a new rule added to a web controller is a fresh violation, not covered by the existing controller-logic deviation.

risks.risk: Unstable ordering. The requirement asks for a stable order for specialties and for the holders under each; two specialties may be stored under the same name, and two veterinarians may share a name.
risks.mitigation: Sort specialties by name with the stored identity as tiebreaker, and holders by last name then first name then identity. Every sort key is total, so the page is deterministic for any data set.

risks.risk: Two specialties stored under one name collapsing into one entry. The narrow reading recorded in the PRD is one entry per stored specialty.
risks.mitigation: Group by the specialty's stored identity, never by its name. Note that Specialty inherits equals/hashCode from the entity hierarchy - if grouping uses a Map keyed by Specialty, confirm the key semantics rather than assuming them, or key by identifier explicitly.

risks.risk: Unbounded read. The page has no paging by requirement and loads every specialty and every veterinarian on each request.
risks.mitigation: Accepted and recorded in the ADR's Consequences. The result set is bounded by the clinic's roster, and the veterinarian read goes through the existing cache. No mitigation is designed in; the risk is stated so a future data-volume change reopens it.

risks.risk: Stale data from the vet cache. VetRepository's reads are cached with no eviction configured (open question 5 in docs/system-design.md).
risks.mitigation: Inherited, not worsened: the directory reads the same cache the vet list already reads, and NG-2 keeps the page read-only with no write path to invalidate. Do not add a specialties cache - that would need a new cache declaration in CacheConfiguration and would widen the same open question.

risks.risk: Build failure from I18nPropertiesSyncTest on hard-coded page text or a key missing from one of the translated bundles.
risks.mitigation: Every visible string goes through #{...}. If a new key is needed, add it to messages.properties and to all nine translated bundles in the same change (messages_en is exempt by fallback).

risks.risk: Lazy-loading failure while rendering, since spring.jpa.open-in-view is disabled.
risks.mitigation: Vet.specialties is mapped FetchType.EAGER, so the graph the page needs is loaded inside the repository call. The read model is assembled before rendering, so the template touches no persistence proxy.
